source_documents.title: Achieving short-wavelength free radical emission by combining small conjugated structure and anti-Kasha emission

reference_evidence_units.quote: calculated to be 0.2% in air and 0.3% in nitrogen after 1 min of light irradiation.
reference_evidence_units.subject: B after irradiation
reference_evidence_units.conditions: B in chloroform, 10 mg/mL; 365 nm, 10 W irradiation for 1 min (p.2 continuation).
reference_evidence_units.statement: Photoactivated B solution has reported PLQYs of 0.2% in air and 0.3% in nitrogen; visible emission persists for about 72 h in the authors' visual assessment.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The approximately 72 h is radical/emission persistence, not excited-state lifetime. A's 1.12 ns value is not assigned to B.

reference_evidence_units.quote: There was no new 1H NMR signal for A in CD3CN and B in CDCl3
reference_evidence_units.subject: Irradiated A and B solutions
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Before/after UV irradiation; NMR and absorption comparison.
reference_evidence_units.statement: No new proton-NMR resonances are reported, while absorption changes indicate a new absorbing species; the authors infer radical generation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Absence of new NMR signals is not unique proof of unchanged chemistry or radical cation identity. B's SI spectra were not inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: A, B, C and D exhibited very weak emission and no obvious photoinduced emission in the solid powder state
reference_evidence_units.subject: A-D powders, including B
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Neat solid powders under light irradiation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Weak powder emission and absence of obvious photoactivation constrain the interpretation: this is polymer-enabled radical luminescence rather than intrinsic AIE.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not infer a specific excimer or exciton from quenching alone. C/D solution negative controls differ from the emitting B solution.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The PLQY of the B-6-PMMA film (the optimum doping concentration) in air was calculated to be 0.7% and 2.0% in nitrogen
reference_evidence_units.subject: B-6-PMMA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Optimum B film; 365 nm, 10 W irradiation for 1 min.
reference_evidence_units.statement: B-PMMA becomes emissive after irradiation, with PLQY 0.7% in air and 2.0% in nitrogen; Fig.3g shows the new blue/green band.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Fig.3g visually inspected; plot legend uses 3 min whereas yield prose uses 1 min. No precise experimental peak or A's 0.92 ns lifetime is assigned to B.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The luminescence intensity of the B-6-PMMA was greatly weakened after heating at 100 ◦C for 30 min
reference_evidence_units.subject: B-6-PMMA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 100 C heating for 30 min, then UV reactivation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Heating weakens radical emission, and photoactivation remains possible over seven heat/light cycles.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Fig.3i visually inspected; Fig.S21 was not inspected. Thermal loss need not uniquely indicate an internal rotor mechanism.

reference_evidence_units.quote: it only showed the slightly change in luminescence
reference_evidence_units.subject: B-6-PMMA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Photoactivated film held in air for 120 h.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The main text reports little luminescence change over 120 h and an FTIR-derived radical conversion estimate of 5.5%, supporting matrix stabilization.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Reported Fig.S19 data were not personally inspected; radical conversion and stability estimates are not direct emission-state identification.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The calculated fluorescence of A and B originates from the anti-Kasha
reference_evidence_units.subject: A and B radical cations
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Quantum-chemical spectra compared with photoactivated films.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Calculated emission is assigned to D4-to-D0 for A at 497 nm and D5-to-D0 for B at 512 nm, not to the neutral precursor singlet fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Table S1 is reported in main text but not inspected. These are state assignments from calculations, not direct state-resolved experimental proof.

reference_evidence_units.quote: making the reason for slow internal conversion due to the large energy gap between corresponding states.
reference_evidence_units.subject: A and B radical cations
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Interpretation of isolated D4(A)/D5(B) states above lower doublets.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors propose that a large gap to lower doublet states slows internal conversion enough to permit higher-doublet fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No experimentally determined internal-conversion rate or complete dynamics is provided in the main-text evidence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: single electron transfer (SET) from dopant to matrix
reference_evidence_units.subject: A and B in PMMA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Photoexcited dopants in a proposed supramolecular complex with PMMA.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The proposed film activation route transfers an electron from excited A/B to PMMA, forming the emissive radical cation; two-step photoionization is the alternative proposed solution route.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: SET is inferred from broad, method-dependent energy-level ranges, not measured electron-transfer kinetics. Figure 4 caption reverses the direction verbally; the mechanistic prose identifies dopant as donor and PMMA as acceptor.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Such supramolecular interactions can protect the free radical from quenching by oxygen and limit the movement of free rad­ icals, leading to free radical emission
reference_evidence_units.subject: A/B radical emitters in PMMA
reference_evidence_units.conditions: PMMA mechanism discussion followed by B-PMMA measurements.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source attributes film stabilization to supramolecular matrix interactions protecting radicals from oxygen and limiting their motion.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The detailed EPR g=2.006 and 1680-to-1685 cm^-1 carbonyl shift are A measurements, not B measurements. Broad radical-motion wording is not direct internal RIM evidence.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: PMMA is proposed to stabilize the photoinduced radicals and reduce quenching; neat-powder and polymer comparisons constrain this environment-specific effect.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Preserve the proposed excited dopant-to-PMMA SET route as an enabling radical-generation mechanism, explicitly distinct from proof of emission-state origin.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The source invokes a high-doublet energy gap slowing IC to lower doublets, allowing radiative competition; no measured rate is asserted.

reference_mechanisms.label: SOKR_ANTI_KASHA
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The proposed D5-to-D0 emission belongs to the photogenerated radical cation, not the neutral legacy precursor. This is theory-supported source interpretation.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: The source invokes protection and restriction of radical movement in PMMA, but does not resolve a specific internal rotational/vibrational suppression mechanism; do not infer RIM from polymer enhancement.

mechanism_decisions.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: PMMA is proposed to stabilize the photoinduced radicals and reduce quenching; neat-powder and polymer comparisons constrain this environment-specific effect.

mechanism_decisions.label: HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No discrete host-guest binding or inclusion mechanism is established; solvent polarity or packing alone does not establish this family.

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific ICT/TICT emissive-state assignment is established in the selected evidence.

mechanism_decisions.label: ESIPT_PT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific excited-state proton-transfer pathway is reported in the selected evidence.

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Preserve the proposed excited dopant-to-PMMA SET route as an enabling radical-generation mechanism, explicitly distinct from proof of emission-state origin.

mechanism_decisions.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Aggregation or close contacts do not by themselves establish an aggregate exciton, excimer, exciplex, or H/J excited state.

mechanism_decisions.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
mechanism_decisions.rationale: The source invokes a high-doublet energy gap slowing IC to lower doublets, allowing radiative competition; no measured rate is asserted.

mechanism_decisions.label: TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No triplet, metal-mediated, or energy-transfer explanation is established for this target by the selected evidence.

mechanism_decisions.label: RACI_CI_ACCESS
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific conical-intersection-mediated decay or restriction of access is established.

mechanism_decisions.label: SOKR_ANTI_KASHA
mechanism_decisions.rationale: The proposed D5-to-D0 emission belongs to the photogenerated radical cation, not the neutral legacy precursor. This is theory-supported source interpretation.
